text:
Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points last week, every one of them in a Stars sweater across 1,274 games, from a fifth-round pick (129th overall in 2007) who went on to win the 2014-15 Art Ross Trophy. That's the story, and it should be.

The hockey right now is a different job. At 37 he plays 12:29 a night with no power-play points, and in that role he's been very good at five-on-five: Dallas gets 57.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 8.9 points better than without him. His 4 goals on 3.8 expected are honest, and the Stars have scored a couple fewer goals than expected with him out there, so his 8 points slightly undersell his shifts.

The thing to watch is the minutes. He played 10:24 in both of the last two games, and our projection of 30 to 48 points assumes something closer to his season average. Evolving-Hockey's one knock last season was penalties: he took more than he drew.
